a flying wing tailsitting vehicle can be controlled in a robust way by a global controller that is based on a model of the dynamics, and that the controller can be implemented on an onboard microcontroller.

a first-principals model of the vehicle, an onboard parameter identification scheme and a cascaded control architecture allow for a global controller for a flying wing tailsiter vehicle that can track nominal trajectories.

we propose a global controller for flying-wing tailsitters that is based on a cascaded control architecture, a first principles model and parameter learning, and that we show that the controller can be implemented on typical microcontrollers and is robust with respect to parameter variations.

the design and implementation of a global controller that is able to track nominal trajectories with a tailsitter vehicle, which is an important capability for the operation of unmanned aerial vehicles.
